sources_considered.why: Randomized evidence of impaired productivity in a specific coding setting.
Independent evaluation of factual reliability in advertised legal research tools.
Evidence of practical benefits from a customer-support deployment; the revised version supplies an exact availability date.
Read to establish the underlying customer-support deployment period rather than treating publication as the event.

evidence_items.explanation: The randomized study establishes a productivity loss in one experienced-developer setting. It does not establish the affected share of all proposed use cases or isolate an inherent architectural cause.

The study finds hallucination rates of 17% to 33% in evaluated legal research tools despite stronger vendor claims. This documents a material reliability problem in a promoted application, but not the fraction of all applications impaired.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Erik Brynjolfsson, Danielle Li, and Lindsey Raymond
evidence_items.explanation: The revised study reports an average 15% productivity gain in customer support, alongside other benefits. The deployment began in late 2020 and expanded in early 2021; this earlier successful application qualifies sweeping extrapolations from failures elsewhere.

The follow-up discusses possible improvements but serious selection and measurement problems. It is later context, not evidence of the state on the post date, and cautions against interpreting the earlier slowdown as a permanent limitation.

unresolved_gaps: No representative denominator of initially promoted use cases was established.
The studies do not estimate the proportion materially undermined.
The evidence does not isolate inherent model design as the cause across the application population.
Early-2025 evaluations cannot alone establish the practical state of every application in December 2025.
